subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A chromatic scale moves entirely in:
questions.explain: A chromatic scale ascends or descends entirely in semitones, using all twelve pitches.

questions.q: The harmonic minor scale differs from the natural minor by raising which note?
questions.explain: The harmonic minor scale raises the seventh note by a semitone, creating a leading note.

questions.q: A minor triad is built from which intervals above the root?
questions.explain: A minor triad stacks a minor 3rd then a major 3rd, giving its darker sound.

questions.q: Rock and pop since the 1960s is most associated with which line-up?
questions.explain: Modern rock and pop is typically built around guitars, bass, drums and vocals.

questions.q: When sequencing in a DAW, individual notes are often arranged on a:
questions.explain: In a DAW, notes are commonly entered and arranged on a piano roll along a track timeline.

questions.q: 'Polyphonic' (or contrapuntal) texture means:
options: Two or more independent melodic lines sounding together
questions.explain: Polyphonic texture combines two or more independent melodic lines.

questions.q: What is the difference between a solo and an ensemble performance?
options: A solo is loud; an ensemble is quiet
A solo is one performer; an ensemble is a group
questions.explain: A solo is performed by one player, while an ensemble involves a group performing together.

questions.q: In the mnemonic 'MAD T-SHIRT' for the elements of music, what does the 'I' stand for?
questions.explain: In 'MAD T-SHIRT' the I stands for instrumentation, meaning the choice of instruments and voices used.

questions.q: What does the dynamic marking 'mezzo-forte' (mf) mean?
questions.explain: Mezzo-forte means moderately loud, sitting between piano and forte.

questions.q: What does a single dot placed after a note do to its value?
options: Adds half the note's value again
questions.explain: A dot after a note increases its length by half of its original value.

questions.q: A triad in 'first inversion' has which note in the bass?
questions.explain: In first inversion the third of the chord is the lowest sounding note.

questions.q: The articulation marking 'staccato' tells a player to make notes:
questions.explain: Staccato means short and detached, the opposite of legato.

questions.q: In a melody-and-accompaniment texture, the accompaniment:
options: Supports the melody with chords or a bass line
questions.explain: The accompaniment supports the main melody, often with chords or a bass line.

questions.q: How many beats does a crotchet last in 4/4 time?
questions.explain: A crotchet lasts one beat in 4/4 time.

questions.q: When structuring a composition, why might a composer reuse a melodic idea in a contrasting section?
options: To create unity while still providing variety
questions.explain: Reusing ideas in new contexts gives a piece unity while contrast keeps it interesting.

questions.q: When performing in an ensemble, watching a conductor or leader mainly helps players to:
options: Stay together in time and respond to changes
questions.explain: Following a conductor or leader keeps the ensemble together in time and unified in expression.

questions.q: A rondo form is best described by which pattern?
questions.explain: In rondo form a main theme (A) returns between contrasting episodes, e.g. ABACA.

questions.q: In a DAW, 'automation' is most commonly used to:
options: Make settings like volume or panning change automatically over time
questions.explain: Automation lets parameters such as volume or panning change automatically across a track over time.

questions.q: Which Italian dynamic term means 'very quiet'?
questions.explain: Pianissimo (pp) means very quiet, whereas fortissimo (ff) means very loud.

questions.q: What does 'a tempo' mean after a passage that has slowed down?
questions.explain: 'A tempo' instructs the performer to return to the original speed after a change.

questions.q: The tempo marking 'andante' indicates a speed that is:
questions.explain: Andante means at a walking pace, a moderate tempo between slow and fast.

questions.q: Using repetition when developing a musical idea helps to:
options: Make ideas memorable and give a sense of unity
questions.explain: Repetition makes musical ideas memorable and gives a piece unity and coherence.
